The Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at Rutgers University-Newark offer the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree program in the mathematical sciences. The graduate faculty provides research opportunities in many fields of specialization, including algebra, 4-manifolds, geometric group theory, Kleinian groups and Teichmüller theory, low-dimensional topology, differential geometry, algebraic geometry, mathematical physics, number theory, and representation theory in pure mathematics. Joint with the Cognitive and Data Science (CoDaS) Lab at Rutgers University-Newark, our program also offers advanced research training in machine learning and modern Artificial Intelligence (AI). The program is designed to provide students major in pure mathematics with a broad and deep knowledge of both classical and modern methods in the mathematical sciences, and provide students major in data science with research training in machine learning and Artificial Intelligence. In addition, students gain experience in applying this knowledge to problems in the sciences and engineering. Individuals entering with a bachelor's degree normally spend their first two years in coursework and in preparation for the Ph.D. qualifying examination. They take that examination no later than fall semester of their third year. Students are encouraged to take a range of courses in both pure and applied mathematics to help decide the research direction they will pursue. The Ph.D. curriculum is divided into two options: pure mathematics and data science. Students in both pure mathematics and data science track are required to take:
1. 26:645:611 Real Analysis I,
2. 26:645:612 Real Analysis II,
3. 26:645:621 Complex Variables I,
4. 26:645:631 Algebra I,
5. 26:645:632 Algebra II,
6. 26:645:641 Topology I,
7. 26:645:642 Topology II, and
8. 26:645:643 Differentiable Manifolds.
The above course requirements can be waived, however, for students with advanced degrees who have completed equivalent coursework.
Additionally, all students are required to take at least 12 credits of advanced elective courses (together with the qualify exam courses, it is total at least 36 credits of courses). These electives are chosen in consultations among the student, the student's adviser, and the advisory committee, and with the permission of the graduate program director.
The Ph.D. qualifying examination for students choosing the pure option consists of five parts, with each part covering the basic topics in a particular subdiscipline.
1. Part A Real analysis,
2. Part B Complex analysis
3. Part C Abstract algebra,
4. Part D Algebraic topology,
5. Part E Differentiable manifold.
After successful completion of the examinations, students begin their doctoral research under the direction of a faculty member. All students are required to take at least 24 credits of doctoral dissertation research (together with credits of courses at least 60 credits). Upon completion, the dissertation is presented to a thesis committee, which conducts a final oral examination. More information about the program, the department, and the faculty may be obtained by visiting the program's website at https://sasn.rutgers.edu/academics-admissions/academic-departments/mathematics-computer-science.
